subject: Banking
title: Buy Now Pay Later
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Buy Now Pay Later.

hook.text: Buy Now Pay Later apps let you split purchases into 4 interest-free payments.

buildup.text: BNPL charges merchants 4-8% per transaction. Merchants pay because BNPL users spend 20-50% more per order.

discovery.text: BNPL is credit without feeling like credit. No credit card application, no interest disclosure, no monthly statements.

twist.text: Late fees and missed payments are rising sharply. Regulators worry BNPL causes debt spirals for young consumers.

climax.text: BNPL hides the psychology of debt behind smooth checkout design. Easy payments mask the risk of overspending.

punchline.text: Four easy payments. Spending rises 20-50%. It is still debt.

quiz.question: Why do merchants accept BNPL's high fees?
options: BNPL users spend 20-50% more per order

details.summary: Buy now, pay later services like Klarna, Afterpay, and Affirm split purchases into interest-free installments at checkout, inserting themselves between traditional credit cards and consumers at the point of sale.
details.whyItMatters: BNPL is reshaping consumer credit by offering instant financing without credit card interest rates. Its rapid growth raises concerns about consumer debt accumulation and regulatory gaps.
takeaways: Purchases are split into four or more interest-free installments
BNPL providers earn revenue from merchant fees, not consumer interest
Late fees and debt accumulation risks are often underestimated

faq.question: How do BNPL companies make money if there is no interest?
faq.answer: Merchants pay BNPL providers 3 to 8 percent of the transaction value because BNPL increases average order sizes and conversion rates. Late payment fees from consumers provide additional revenue.

faq.question: Does BNPL affect your credit score?
faq.answer: Increasingly, yes. Major BNPL providers now report to credit bureaus. Missed payments can damage your score, and having many BNPL accounts may signal financial stress to traditional lenders.
